plan.topic: Survodutide's 13.1% result in type 2 diabetes, decoded: why weight loss is lower in T2D on every GLP-1-type drug
plan.angle: Title: 'Survodutide in Type 2 Diabetes: Why 13.1% Didn't Impress Investors #shorts'. Within 10s: '13.1% is the top dose for people who stayed on treatment, vs 3.1% on placebo. Counting everyone, it's about 10% vs 4%.' On-screen qualifier: 'top dose · if stayed on treatment · 76 wks · adults with T2D + obesity/overweight · investigational, not approved as of Oct 2026'. Key idea: in every major trial of this drug class so far, people with type 2 diabetes lose less weight than people without it. Only compare against T2D trials (e.g. tirzepatide SURMOUNT-2, retatrutide TRIUMPH-2), labelled as separate trials with no head-to-head. Attribute the 'disappointment' to investors: 'Zealand shares fell about 11%. Analysts pointed to side effects.' One line: 'stomach side effects in about 3 in 4 vs about 4 in 10 on placebo, mostly mild to moderate.' Point viewers to the full video. Close with: 'It's a prescription medicine. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.' 35–50s.
plan.why: Spin-off of L1. A headline decoder that names the drug while the news is fresh drives traffic to the long-form video. | fact-check: Same estimand problem as L1. 13.1% vs 3.1% is the efficacy estimand ('if people stayed on treatment'). NEJM's headline figures are −9.8% (6.0 mg) / −8.2% (3.6 mg) vs −3.9% placebo at 76 weeks. A 13.1% stat pill without its estimand breaks the 'verified number, not press-release up to' rule. 'Lower on every drug in this class' is too absolute. The trial pattern is consistent (STEP 2 vs STEP 1, SURMOUNT-2 vs SURMOUNT-1, SYNCHRONIZE-2 vs SYNCHRONIZE-1, TRIUMPH-2), but say 'in every major trial so far'. 'Markets shrugged' must be attributed: Zealand shares fell about 11% on 1 Oct, with analysts citing tolerability (Bloomberg, Fierce Biotech). The GI rate is confirmed: 72.8–77.7% vs 38.6% on placebo.

package.title: Survodutide's 13.1% Weight Loss in T2D: Unimpressed? #shorts
package.description:
Survodutide: 13.1% weight loss (top dose, if people stayed on treatment) vs 3.1% on placebo in adults with type 2 diabetes and overweight or obesity over 76 weeks. Counting everyone: about 10% vs 4%. The type 2 diabetes catch: in big semaglutide and tirzepatide trials, people with T2D lost less weight. Tirzepatide's top dose: about 21% without diabetes vs about 15% with it, placebo about 3% (separate trials, none head-to-head with survodutide). Stomach side effects: about 3 in 4 vs 4 in 10 on placebo, mostly mild to moderate; about 18% stopped because of them (vs about 1% on placebo). Partner Zealand Pharma's shares fell about 11%.

#GLP1 #Survodutide #TypeTwoDiabetes #ClinicalTrial

This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice. Always talk to a qualified healthcare professional about your own situation. Survodutide isn't approved yet. GLP-1 medicines are prescription medicines. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether one is right for you.

script.working_title: Survodutide in Type 2 Diabetes: Why 'Up to 13.1%' Didn't Impress Investors #shorts
script.hook_pattern: Headline decoder: a named drug, the headline number framed as 'up to', and a surprising investor reaction ("up to 13.1%… so why weren't investors impressed?"). Within 10 seconds the viewer hears both ways of counting, each with its placebo figure. The answer comes in three parts: an attributed BMO comment, the rate of stopping for side effects, and a benchmark from a separate diabetes trial.

factcheck.summary: The core claims check out. SYNCHRONIZE-2 (NCT06066528, NEJM 2026): 752 adults with type 2 diabetes and BMI 27+, 76 weeks, survodutide 3.6 mg or 6.0 mg vs placebo. Top dose: 13.1% vs 3.1% if people stayed on treatment, and 9.8% vs 3.9% counting everyone randomised. Stomach side effects were 72.8% / 77.7% vs 38.6%, mostly mild to moderate. 18% vs 1.2% stopped because of them. Fierce Biotech (1 Oct 2026) confirms the ~11% fall in Zealand shares and BMO's line: 'a less competitive profile vs other agents'. The tirzepatide benchmarks count everyone, which matches survodutide's ~10%: SURMOUNT-1 20.9% vs 3.1%, and SURMOUNT-2 14.7% vs 3.2%, both 72 weeks. They are labelled as separate trials and not head-to-head. Every rate has its placebo figure, both ways of counting are given, approval status is date-hedged and the prescriber line is there. Nothing is unsafe. Remaining issues are minor wording fixes: attribute the 'up to', keep overweight/obesity on screen, attribute the 'looked modest' inference, and use the exact prescriber line. I couldn't open the NEJM page (403) or the ClinicalTrials.gov record (didn't render). I confirmed both through PubMed/NEJM search results and the Boehringer press release, and checked the NEJM numbers through secondary reports (Medical Dialogues, AJMC).

issues.claim: Survodutide: up to 13.1% weight loss in type 2 diabetes.
issues.problem: The 'up to' wording comes from the press release but isn't attributed. Our rules say to use the verified number rather than the press-release 'up to', unless it's attributed. Scene 2 does decode it within seconds, so this is minor.
issues.fix: Boehringer says survodutide gave 'up to 13.1%' weight loss in type 2 diabetes. So why weren't investors impressed?

issues.problem: The on-screen text drops 'overweight or obesity', which the narration includes. That narrows the population on screen, and we've had scope errors before.
NEJM reports 752 participants (250/251/251). The press release says 755. 'Treated' isn't the paper's word.
issues.fix: top dose · if stayed on treatment · 76 wks · 752 adults with T2D + overweight/obesity (BMI 27+) · placebo 3.1% · investigational, not approved as of Oct 2026

issues.claim: Next to that diabetes-trial benchmark, about 10% looked modest.
issues.problem: This comparison is our reading, not a reason the investors gave. BMO only said 'less competitive profile vs other agents'. It needs to be clearly framed as context so it doesn't read as the investors' stated reason.
issues.fix: Tirzepatide's top dose: about 21% without diabetes, 15% with it, placebo about 3%. Separate trials, none head-to-head with survodutide. Next to that diabetes-trial benchmark, survodutide's about 10% looks modest.

issues.claim: GLP-1 medicines are prescription medicines. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether one is right for you.
issues.problem: The wording is close to the required prescriber line but not exact.
issues.fix: Full breakdown on our channel. Survodutide isn't approved yet, as of October 2026. GLP-1 medicines are prescription medicines. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether one is right for you.

issues.claim: about 18% stopped because of them, vs about 1% on placebo
issues.problem: This is accurate: Boehringer reports 18% vs 1.2% stopping because of stomach side effects. Fierce Biotech also reports that 26% stopped because of any side effect, but I couldn't confirm that figure in the paper. Don't add it unless the NEJM paper confirms it. You could add that most people who stopped did so while the dose was being increased, which Boehringer and AJMC both report.
